transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?
I’m here because… after I eat too much, I’ve been making myself throw up in the bathroom so I don’t gain weight. It’s gotten bad, and I’m honestly scared I can’t stop doing it.
Do you feel that your weight or shape has a big impact on how you see yourself or your self-worth?

Yeah… it does. More than I’d like to admit. If my work pants feel tight, or I see my stomach in the mirror, it’s like my whole opinion of myself drops. I start feeling like I’m failing at everything, not just my body. Like I’m not that strong woman who can handle transmissions and keep up with the guys anymore.
Do you ever find yourself eating a lot in one sitting — more than most people would eat in the same amount of time — and feeling like you can’t stop once you start?

Yeah. Mostly at night, once the house is quiet, I’ll end up in the kitchen and just start eating whatever’s there—leftovers, cereal, chips, ice cream. It goes way past a normal meal, and I keep going even when I know it’s too much. Sometimes it feels like half the pantry’s been picked through before I stop.
When you're eating like that in the evening, do you feel like you can't control how much you're eating — like you can't stop once you start?

Yeah. Once I start, it feels like I’m not really in control. I’ll be telling myself, “Lucy, stop, that’s enough,” but my hands just keep grabbing more food. I don’t really feel back in charge until after it’s over.
How often have you been making yourself throw up after eating too much — would you say it happens at least once a week, or more often?

Yeah… it’s at least once a week. Honestly, for the last three months or so, I don’t think there’s been many weeks where it didn’t happen after one of those late-night eating episodes. Some weeks it’s several times, especially if I’m home more because of my back.
